items.name: low dose aspirin 81 mg, 120 count
items.note: OTC medicines are medical care for FSAs and HRAs whether or not prescribed; CARES Act §3702 removed the prescription-only limit for expenses after 2019.

items.name: infant ibuprofen drops, 1 oz
items.note: Children's OTC medicines are OTC medicines, eligible after 2019.

items.name: saline solution, 12 oz
items.note: Equipment and materials required for using contact lenses, such as saline solution and enzyme cleaner, are includible.

items.name: adult multivitamin, 100 count
items.note: Vitamins and supplements aren't includible unless recommended by a medical practitioner as treatment for a specific diagnosed condition.

items.name: baby diapers size 3, 84 count
items.note: Diapers aren't includible unless needed to relieve the effects of a particular disease; ordinary baby diapers are not.

items.name: bladder control pads, moderate, 54 count
items.note: Diapers are excluded unless needed to relieve the effects of a particular disease; adult incontinence products qualify when used for a medical condition.

items.name: pseudoephedrine 12-hour decongestant, 10 count
items.note: Cold, flu and cough medicines are OTC medicines, eligible without a prescription after 2019.

items.name: overnight maxi pads, 28 count
items.note: Menstrual care products (tampon, pad, liner, cup, sponge or similar) are treated as medical care for HSAs, FSAs and HRAs after 2019.

items.name: loratadine 10 mg, 30 count
items.note: Allergy medicines are OTC medicines, eligible without a prescription after 2019.
